content.user_title: Build Federal SOW and PWS Documents
content.value_statement: Federal acquisition teams need measurable requirements without mixing pricing content into the contract document. This skill builds structured SOW or PWS files and separate internal handoffs.
actual_capabilities: Guides intake for document form, contract framework, scope, period, quality, security, and transition.
Builds a new SOW or PWS, converts an SOO, or reduces scope in an existing requirements document.
Structures measurable requirements, deliverables, acceptance criteria, performance standards, and AQLs.
Produces separate chat-only staffing and Section B handoffs without placing pricing details in the contract document.
Validates DOCX structure, required sections, dynamic TOC settings, and prohibited content leakage.
limitations: Does not create an IGCE, acquisition plan, market research report, clause matrix, or standalone QASP.
Requires user or Contracting Officer confirmation for contract type, commerciality, and CPFF form decisions.
Requires local DOCX authoring and office rendering capabilities for the complete workflow.
Does not process classified information or replace legal, policy, or Contracting Officer review.

use_cases.title: Draft a New PWS
use_cases.description: Turn program requirements into outcome-based objectives, standards, AQLs, deliverables, and acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Convert an SOO
use_cases.description: Extract settled objectives and identify missing decisions before producing an executable SOW or PWS.

use_cases.title: Reduce Contract Scope
use_cases.description: Compare current requirements with budget constraints and revise selected capabilities while preserving internal staffing assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic PWS
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a PWS for [service]. The agency is [agency], users are [population], and performance occurs at [location]. Begin with the required intake questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when starting from a short service description.

prompt_templates.title: Draft from Detailed Requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [SOW or PWS] from these requirements: [requirements]. The confirmed contract framework is [type], and the period is [period]. Stop at each approval gate.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the main scope and acquisition decisions are available.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Source Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert the attached SOO into a [SOW or PWS]. Preserve settled facts, list unresolved decisions, and keep staffing and Section B details outside the DOCX.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when objectives already exist in an SOO.

prompt_templates.title: Perform a Controlled Scope Reduction
prompt_templates.prompt: Revise the attached [SOW or PWS] to meet a target of [budget or coverage]. Present capability tradeoffs first, wait for selection, then update the document and handoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a budget-driven revision of an existing requirement.

output_examples.input: Create a PWS for a 24-hour federal help desk with measurable service levels.
output: A DOCX PWS organized around service outcomes, response standards, AQLs, deliverables, security, transition, and a QASP summary.
A separate staffing handoff showing the approved coverage basis.
A separate Section B handoff with suggested line-item structure.

output_examples.input: Convert an agency SOO for application modernization into a contract-ready SOW.
output_examples.output: A structured SOW that preserves supplied objectives, resolves scope gaps through approval questions, and defines testable tasks and acceptance criteria.

output_examples.input: Reduce an existing PWS while protecting essential incident response coverage.
output_examples.output: A revised PWS reflecting approved capability tradeoffs, plus updated internal staffing and Section B handoffs that remain outside the contract file.

best_practices: Provide known scope, workload, service levels, period, location, security context, and agency templates before drafting.
Confirm staffing assumptions and the Decision Summary before document generation.
Have the Contracting Officer review contract framework, clauses, Section B structure, and unresolved assumptions.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to choose a contract type, commerciality determination, or CPFF form.
Do not place staffing counts, SOC codes, CLINs, rates, or pricing schedules inside the SOW or PWS.
Do not treat LibreOffice rendering or automated validation as proof of Microsoft Word behavior.

faq.question: What documents can this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates federal SOW or PWS DOCX files and supports SOO conversion and controlled scope reduction.

faq.question: Does it create an IGCE?
faq.answer: No. It creates a chat-only staffing handoff that a separate pricing or IGCE workflow can use.

faq.question: Can it select the contract type?
faq.answer: No. It explains document consequences but requires the user or Contracting Officer to confirm the contract framework.

faq.question: Where do CLIN and pricing details appear?
faq.answer: They appear only in a chat-only Section B handoff, never in the SOW or PWS body.

faq.question: How does it validate the DOCX?
faq.answer: It checks package structure, section order, headings, TOC settings, measurable content, and prohibited information leakage.

faq.question: Does it replace acquisition or legal review?
faq.answer: No. A qualified reviewer must verify regulatory citations, agency requirements, assumptions, security language, and final acquisition decisions.
